metadata.title: Naoki Matsui | Institute of Science Tokyo | Solid-State Battery & Solid Ionics Research
metadata.description: Battery research laboratory at Institute of Science Tokyo (Kanno-Suzuki-Matsui Lab, Dr. Naoki Matsui), working on all-solid-state lithium batteries, lithium-ion conductors, fluoride batteries, hydride-ion conductors, and other next-generation battery materials.

researchDetails.title: RESEARCH DETAILS
researchDetails.subtitle: Our research topics in detail
researchDetails.fluorideDesc1: Fluoride batteries are attracting attention as next-generation energy storage devices with a higher theoretical energy density than lithium batteries. Realizing them requires solid electrolytes in which fluoride ions can move rapidly through the solid.
researchDetails.fluorideDesc2: We search for new fluoride ion conductors and work to clarify their conduction mechanisms. In particular, we are developing solid electrolytes that combine electrochemical stability with ionic conductivity, as well as lone-pair-containing fluoride ion conductors that show extremely high ionic conductivity.
researchDetails.lithiumDesc: Putting all-solid-state lithium-ion batteries into practical use urgently requires new solid electrolytes that combine high ionic conductivity with chemical stability. We search for such materials efficiently by combining materials informatics with experiments.
researchDetails.hydrideTitle: Exploration of Hydride Ion Conducting Materials and Devices
researchDetails.hydrideDesc: We are developing new energy devices that use hydride ions (H⁻), the negative ions of hydrogen, as charge carriers. Hydride ion conductors are expected to enable new battery systems that exploit the fast conduction and unique reactivity of hydride ions.
researchDetails.anionDesc: In contrast to conventional cation (Li⁺, Na⁺, etc.) intercalation, we are developing electrode materials into which anions (F⁻, Cl⁻, etc.) are reversibly inserted and extracted. By building new battery systems, we aim to achieve higher energy densities.
researchDetails.mlTitle: Exploration Using Machine Learning and Virtual Space
researchDetails.mlDesc: Combining materials informatics and computational chemistry, we develop machine-learning methods to search for new ion conductors efficiently. Designing materials from both the experimental and theoretical sides makes conventional trial-and-error searches far more efficient.
researchDetails.htsDesc: By combining combinatorial synthesis with high-throughput evaluation, we explore materials far faster than conventional methods allow. Synthesizing and evaluating many compositions at once greatly raises the chance of discovering new materials.

profile.philosophyText1: I believe that breakthroughs in energy storage technology come from a deep understanding of the fundamental mechanisms governing ion transport in solids.
profile.philosophyText2: By integrating experimental synthesis, advanced characterization techniques, and computational approaches, I aim to design materials that enable safe, high-performance next-generation batteries for a sustainable future.
profile.hobbiesText1: Outside of research, I enjoy rugby and walking. Time spent exercising is also a good chance to think up new research ideas.
profile.hobbiesText2: I also keep learning about related fields (materials informatics, electrochemistry, structural analysis) and look for ways to apply them to materials science.
